anti_patterns.mistake: Unchecked npx execution polluting JSON-RPC stdout with colored notices and ANSI escape sequences
anti_patterns.root_cause: npx in modern npm writes colored notices to stdout when not silenced, breaking JSON-RPC parsing (invalid character '\x1b')
anti_patterns.strategy: Always wrap Node-based MCP servers using mcp-npx with NO_COLOR=1, npm_config_loglevel=silent, and --silent flag
anti_patterns.invariant_rule: NEVER run raw npx for MCP STDIO processes; always use mcp-npx wrapper.

anti_patterns.mistake: Sentry MCP server falling back to interactive OAuth device code flow and hanging
anti_patterns.root_cause: @sentry/mcp-server defaults to interactive device code login if --access-token or SENTRY_ACCESS_TOKEN is omitted
anti_patterns.strategy: Pass --access-token ${SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN} explicitly in CLI arguments and provide environment fallback
anti_patterns.invariant_rule: Always explicitly supply auth tokens via CLI flags when MCP server defaults to interactive browser/device-code login.

anti_patterns.mistake: Codebase indexer scanning self-extracting archive payload and inflating codebase database to 40MB+
anti_patterns.root_cause: Scanning binary payloads or packed archive files in analyze.py treats binary blobs as source text
anti_patterns.strategy: Exclude *.tar.gz, *.tar.xz, install.sh, and dist/ in codebase indexing routines
anti_patterns.invariant_rule: Always configure self-exclusion lists in static analyzers and file crawlers for binary/build artifacts.

anti_patterns.mistake: Leaving MCP servers running permanently in background consuming CPU and RAM
anti_patterns.root_cause: Static mcp_config.json with default background servers creates memory bloat and port collisions
anti_patterns.strategy: Zero-Default profile: start with empty mcpServers ({}), enable dynamically on-demand, and auto-close upon task completion
anti_patterns.invariant_rule: Default mcp_config.json must remain empty (0 active servers). Enable servers dynamically and disable immediately after turn.

anti_patterns.mistake: Agent looping over view_file sequentially to understand an entire folder codebase
anti_patterns.root_cause: Sequential view_file calls waste context tokens and cause high latency
anti_patterns.strategy: Execute analyze.py --check --auto-heal --inject-ki and read the consolidated codebase_summary.md in a single read
anti_patterns.invariant_rule: NEVER call view_file recursively across multiple files in a folder; use codebase_summary.md.

anti_patterns.mistake: Refactoring code outside the user's requested scope
anti_patterns.root_cause: Agent interprets adjacent code as needing improvement or unsolicited optimization.
anti_patterns.strategy: Blast Radius Lock: Declare edit scope upfront; only edit within declared scope; flag out-of-scope issues as follow-up recommendations.
anti_patterns.invariant_rule: Never touch or refactor files or functions outside the declared blast radius without explicit user authorization.

anti_patterns.mistake: Claiming success without running verification commands
anti_patterns.root_cause: Token-pressure or speed bias leads agent to skip test runs and pattern-match 'this looks right' or use speculative language.
anti_patterns.strategy: Evidence Gate: Always run tests or re-read files, report actual terminal output, never say 'should work'.
anti_patterns.invariant_rule: Zero speculative claims: every declaration of success requires empirical terminal execution evidence.

anti_patterns.mistake: Editing files based on stale cached memory instead of current on-disk state
anti_patterns.root_cause: Files read early in long sessions get modified externally or by background tasks while agent remembers old lines.
anti_patterns.strategy: Freshness Gate: Re-read target file if >5 tool calls since last read; run git status before multi-file edits.
anti_patterns.invariant_rule: Always re-read target files before applying diffs if >5 tool calls elapsed or external changes occurred.

anti_patterns.mistake: Using invented library functions that don't exist in installed packages
anti_patterns.root_cause: LLM hallucination on fast-moving libraries or niche frameworks where training memory contains plausible APIs.
anti_patterns.strategy: Hallucination Guard: Verify every unfamiliar API symbol via tool inspection, REPL check, or docs before using.
anti_patterns.invariant_rule: Verify all library APIs and methods via tools before writing code; pass Import Verification Gate.

anti_patterns.mistake: Polling in loops or setting redundant timers while waiting for background tasks or command completion
anti_patterns.root_cause: Failing to utilize the system's reactive wakeup and task notification event loop, resulting in busy-wait polling and wasted timer wakeups
anti_patterns.strategy: Always use 'Waiting for a task notification' with live status. Avoid unnecessary timers; do not poll; stop calling tools and await direct completion signal
anti_patterns.invariant_rule: NEVER poll or loop on task status; rely on reactive task completion notifications with live status and avoid unneeded timers.

anti_patterns.mistake: Reading a single file in multiple sliced chunks or piecemeal line ranges when analyzing it
anti_patterns.root_cause: Unnecessary line range slicing on single-file analysis resulting in fragmented context and multiple redundant tool calls
anti_patterns.strategy: When a single file needs to be analyzed, read the entire file in one call (single view_file without line slicing)
anti_patterns.invariant_rule: Always read a target file in its entirety in a single call when analyzing that file.

anti_patterns.mistake: Suboptimal or haphazard tool selection resulting in excessive latency, token waste, or context bloat
anti_patterns.root_cause: Executing operations reflexively using generic shell commands or piecemeal calls without pre-evaluating the optimal specialized tool
anti_patterns.strategy: Pre-Flight Tool Evaluation: Consciously select the most direct tool (grep_search over shell search, view_file over cat, multi_replace over fragmented edits, reactive async task over polling) before initiating execution
anti_patterns.invariant_rule: Always determine and select the optimal tool for time, context, and execution efficiency before starting execution.

anti_patterns.mistake: Adding extraneous YAML frontmatter keys (disable-model-invocation, metadata, license) or mismatched name fields to workflows, or syncing global workflows only to ~/.gemini/config/workflows/
anti_patterns.root_cause: Antigravity IDE expects strict description-only frontmatter matching the filename stem, and native global workflow discovery watches ~/.gemini/antigravity-ide/global_workflows/
anti_patterns.strategy: Workflows must strictly contain description-only YAML frontmatter matching their file stems, and global workflows must dual-sync to ~/.gemini/antigravity-ide/global_workflows/ and ~/.gemini/config/workflows/
anti_patterns.invariant_rule: Maintain strict description-only frontmatter in all workflows and dual-sync global workflows to ~/.gemini/antigravity-ide/global_workflows/.

anti_patterns.mistake: Invoking generic shell commands, sliced reads, or polling loops instead of specialized tool primitives
anti_patterns.root_cause: Omitting pre-flight goal, task, and context analysis, leading to unbounded token blowouts, multi-turn latency, and broken shell quoting
anti_patterns.strategy: Pre-Execution Tool Optimization: Evaluate represented goal, task, and context to select the exact optimal primitive (grep_search for search, full view_file for inspection, multi_replace_file_content for batch edits, tuned run_command for sync execution, reactive wakeup for async tasks)
anti_patterns.invariant_rule: Always evaluate and dispatch the optimal, lowest-token, highest-velocity primitive before taking action.

anti_patterns.mistake: Reinventing ad-hoc procedures or ignoring existing domain workflows (e.g. /webperf, /debug, /design-ui, /reach, /yagni-simplify) when a task matches them, or dumping entire workflow text into the conversation context
anti_patterns.root_cause: Failing to recognize task domain patterns, or loading workflows verbosely rather than reading and executing on-demand
anti_patterns.strategy: Context-Driven Workflow Adaptation: Match the task domain to the specialized ZeroGravity workflow, read on-demand in a single view_file call, and execute its checklist directly without conversational preamble
anti_patterns.invariant_rule: Always adopt specialized domain workflows when context warrants, loaded strictly on-demand without context bloat.

anti_patterns.mistake: Agent executing Python scripts (analyze.py, auto_evolve.py, checklist.py, harness.py, ki_injector.py, learn.py, mcp.py, session_manager.py, summarizer.py, sync_knowledge.py) for internal memory updates, context sweeps, or configuration tasks
anti_patterns.root_cause: Spawning subprocesses consumes 400-800 tokens per call, creates shell escape issues, adds process startup latency, and bypasses native IDE primitives
anti_patterns.strategy: Strictly use integrated IDE tools (view_file, write_to_file, replace_file_content, multi_replace_file_content, grep_search, ask_question) directly for all memory, configuration, checklist, and context operations
anti_patterns.invariant_rule: NEVER invoke internal Python scripts for agent memory, checklist, or context tasks; use native integrated file and search tools.

anti_patterns.mistake: Performing specialized domain tasks (accessibility, Chrome DevTools testing, HF Hub operations, performance audits) without inspecting and activating the matching available skill
anti_patterns.root_cause: Improvising ad-hoc actions or generic guesses instead of checking the progressive disclosure skill catalog and reading SKILL.md
anti_patterns.strategy: Context-Driven Skill Auto-Activation: Identify matching available skills from the index, inspect SKILL.md in a single view_file call, and execute following its documented workflows and runbooks
anti_patterns.invariant_rule: Always inspect and follow the matching SKILL.md before executing specialized domain tasks.

anti_patterns.mistake: Opening multiple independent IDE windows instead of unified multi-root workspace causing system memory exhaustion and swap lag
anti_patterns.root_cause: Multiple Electron instances duplicate renderers, extension hosts, and language servers, exhausting RAM and triggering slow disk swap thrashing
anti_patterns.strategy: Consolidate active projects into a single multi-root workspace using ide-open, prune stale processes with ide-prune, and expand ZRAM to 12GB
anti_patterns.invariant_rule: Consolidate concurrent development projects into unified multi-root workspaces to avoid Electron process multiplication.
